Krizevci New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Križevci, Croatia

Not demolished. Križevci was, according to local tradition, a foundational site in the defense of Croatian statehood. Jewish merchants first visited in the 16th century, settling from Moravia and Austria, though a 1729 ban initially forced them to settle in nearby villages rather than the town itself. A synagogue costing 45,000 forints was built in 1895, and Rabbi Leopold Leib served the community from 1866 to 1895. After the Holocaust, during which the synagogue was desecrated and looted and local Jews sent to concentration camps, only 9 Jews returned; local authorities never restored the synagogue to the Jewish community, converting it instead into a House of Culture — today a tourist center. This cemetery, established in 1899 as part of the new municipal cemetery, holds about 100 monuments inscribed in German, Hebrew, and Croatian, with burials ranging from 1895 to as late as 2004, and includes five adjacent family ohels with burials dating between 1920 and 1938.
